prompt: RimWorld top-down game animal sprite: the bokka, a small armoured quadruped reptile of the arid desert. FOUR visible legs with clawed feet, a tail, and heavy jowls -- its engine body is QuadrupedAnimalWithClawsTailAndJowl and its weapons are left and right claws, so limbs, claws and tail must all read clearly. Hind legs are NOTICEABLY LONGER than the forelegs, a digging and burrowing build. Thick durable plated hide in a dry desert palette of dust-browns and ochres. Looks engineered for heat and for going underground. No Earth-nameable silhouette -- not an iguana, not a monitor lizard, not a tortoise, and NOT a rock or boulder shape. Painterly rendered game art with real volume and specular highlight, not a flat cartoon outline.
style_notes: REPLACES donor art that depicts the WRONG ANIMAL. The outgoing Stoneback_*.png are Biomes! Caverns' stone-mimic concept, inherited unchanged at the port: a legless brown mound with a single dot eye and flat cartoon fill. Our def is the BOKKA -- baseBodySize 0.4, body QuadrupedAnimalWithClawsTailAndJowl, tools left claw / right claw, description says longer back legs and lives underground. Legs, claws and tail are the whole point of this regen; a rounded legless silhouette is a FAIL. Second defect: flat cartoon styling (uniform heavy outline, radial-gradient fill) against the painterly rendered volume of current art in the same folder tree, e.g. ShatterJaw. NOTE ON CANVAS: kept at 256x256 deliberately. An earlier reading of this called 256 sub-standard because 5 of the 8 newest sprites are 512 -- that was WRONG. MEASURED across this mod: canvas does not track recency, and for drawSize-1 creatures 256 is the convention (16 files at 256 against 2 at 512), consistent with the drawSize x 128 ceiling the queue itself warns on. Owner asked a judgement, not a regen: "Arid biome approved, make sure our art is up to modern standards." It was judged by looking, and it fell short on identity and style, NOT on resolution. Do NOT swap the result in silently; cosmetic changes need his permission.
